text: Johnson Evan Gicheru (died 25 December 2020)[1][2] was a Kenyan lawyer and the 12th Chief Justice of the Republic of Kenya.[3] He was appointed by President Mwai Kibaki following his election in 2003 and served as Chief Justice from 21 February 2003 until his retirement on 27 February 2011, making him the longest-serving African Chief Justice in Kenya's history. He held various early career positions, including Senior State Counsel in the Office of the Attorney General and administrative officer in the Office of the President. He was appointed a Judge of the High Court in 1982 and became a member of the Court of Appeal on 8 June 1988. During his tenure, he served as chairperson of a judicial inquiry into the death of Foreign Affairs Minister Robert Ouko, though the commission was disbanded before releasing its findings.[4] He was married to Mrs. Margaret Gicheru and they had seven children.[5] Johnson Evan Gicheru passed away on 25 December 2020.
